title: The Ride Back
summary: Written against the measurement rather than around it. Movement lives in SILENT shots -- I2V with no dialogue, which produced motion 12.1 and travel 42.3 against S2V's best of 5.7 -- and dialogue lives in its own shots. That is how animation is cut anyway: you rarely hear someone speak while they cross a room in a wide. Six of eleven shots carry no dialogue at all and exist purely to move.

scenes.visual: Wide shot. The warrior walks from the left of the frame to the right, crossing the valley with long strides, cloak trailing. He does not stop.
Medium shot from the waist up. The princess watches him go. Static camera.

dialogue.line: He did not look back. I had thought he would look back.

scenes.visual: Wide shot. The warrior walks from the left of the frame toward the right along the clifftop, long strides, wind in his cloak.
Three-quarter shot from the waist up, the warrior stopped at the edge, sea behind him. Static camera.

dialogue.line: The horse knows the way better than I do. She has done it before.

scenes.visual: Very wide shot. The warrior walks from the left of the frame to the right across the sunlit water, long steady strides. He does not stop.
Very wide shot of the open ocean at golden hour, a blazing path of sunlight running to a wall of golden mist. No people.
Three-quarter shot from the waist up, low sun on his face, calm bright water behind. Static camera.

dialogue.line: Three hundred years. I have been saying the number for a day and it still means nothing.

scenes.visual: Wide shot of the collapsed mossy ring-fort under flat grey overcast, bare thorn trees, wet ground. No people.
Wide shot. The warrior walks forward between the fallen stones toward camera, slowly, looking up at the ruin as he comes.
Close shot. The warrior's face, grey light on him, taking in what is in front of him. Static camera.

dialogue.line: I knew the hall would be gone. I did not know the hill would look smaller.

scenes.visual: Wide shot. The warrior walks from the right of the frame to the left, crossing between the fallen stones with long strides. He does not stop.
